children: Macy's is scheduled to report its second-quarter financial results before the market opens on Thursday. Here is what to know.
SALES: The department-store chain is expected to report $4.81 billion in sales, matching the $4.81 billion in the prior-year quarter, according to FactSet.
PROFIT: The New York company is expected to post a profit of $95.1 million, compared with a profit of $87 million the year before, according to FactSet.
ADJUSTED EARNINGS PER SHARE: Adjusted earnings are expected to come in at 37 cents a share, compared with 41 a share in the prior-year period.
The stock has gained 2% this year, and recently traded at $22.27.

Investor sentiment is already fairly conservative when it comes to department store retailers, and UBS analysts don't expect Macy's report to move the stock meaningfully. They expect Macy's will raise its full-year earnings per share view, and they expect third-quarter guidance will be in line with Wall Street estimates.

Macy's management said back in June that the second quarter was on an encouraging track that was consistent with the company's first-quarter performance. JPMorgan analysts think the consumer was resilient through the quarter, based on their research. They also think Macy's could benefit from the World Cup during the quarter, as tourism demand has historically been a tailwind for the retailer.

Big-box retailers have been a mixed bag when it comes to second-quarter performance. While Target's results impressed investors, Walmart disappointed and said it was investing more in its lowest-cost items to win back low-income shoppers. Kohl's said its customers were feeling pressured by high gas prices, making them more cautious about discretionary spending.
